Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Economic Policy
The manifesto proposes an industrial strategy focused on renewable energy, digital and bioscience sectors. Key measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expanding the British Business Bank, creating Lifelong Skills Grants (£5,000 per adult), and reforming the apprenticeship levy into a broader skills levy. Tax proposals include increasing the Digital Services Tax from 2% to 6%, reforming capital gains tax, and introducing a 4% tax on FTSE-100 share buybacks.

## Healthcare
The party commits to guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) by recruiting 8,000 additional GPs. Additional proposals include reforming NHS dental contracts, establishing mental health hubs for young people, guaranteeing cancer treatment within 62 days of urgent referral, and introducing free personal care based on the Scottish model.

## Social Care
Plans include creating a National Care Agency to set standards, increasing Carer's Allowance eligibility, introducing a £2/hour "Carer's Minimum Wage" premium, establishing a Royal College of Care Workers, and providing statutory respite break guarantees for unpaid carers.

## Education
Proposals include placing mental health professionals in every school, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, introducing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, reinstating maintenance grants for students, and establishing a commission to reform qualifications and curriculum.

## Housing
The manifesto targets building 380,000 homes annually including 150,000 social homes, creating ten new garden cities, banning no-fault evictions, implementing three-year default tenancies, abolishing residential leaseholds, and introducing "Rent to Own" schemes for social housing.

## Environment
Environmental commitments include achieving net zero by 2045, generating 90% renewable electricity by 2030, launching emergency home insulation programmes, banning water company sewage dumping, planting 60 million trees annually, and passing a Clean Air Act based on WHO guidelines.

## Transport
Plans include reinstating the 2030 zero-emission vehicle requirement, freezing rail fares, extending rail electrification, giving local authorities bus franchising powers, and investing in cycling and walking infrastructure.

## Immigration and Asylum
The party would repeal the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme, process asylum claims within three months, allow asylum seekers to work after three months, expand Youth Mobility Schemes with the EU, and create new humanitarian visa routes.

## Constitutional Reform
Proposals include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, extending voting rights to 16-17 year olds, scrapping voter ID requirements, capping political donations, enshrining the Ministerial Code in law, and reforming the House of Lords.

## Defence and International
The manifesto commits to reversing army cuts with ambitions to exceed 100,000 troops, increasing defence spending toward 2.5% of GDP, maintaining nuclear deterrent, restoring 0.7% international development spending, re-establishing an independent development department, and pursuing closer EU relations including eventual Single Market membership.
